title: Reject invalid catalog pagination before querying the database
prompt:
Fix only src/app/api/bazaar/catalog/route.ts and add tests/catalog-pagination.test.mjs. Evidence: src/app/api/bazaar/catalog/route.ts:7-8 uses parseInt without validating finite, nonnegative integers, then line 38 passes the values directly into the database range. Executing GET with a mocked query and ?limit=abc&offset=-2 passed [-2, NaN] to range. API consumers get database-dependent failures rather than a clear client error; fractional and partially numeric strings are also silently truncated.

Validate supplied pagination parameters before obtaining the database client. Keep absent limit/offset defaults of 50/0 and the existing maximum limit of 100. Require a positive safe integer limit and a nonnegative safe integer offset, reject empty or malformed supplied strings with HTTP 400 and a useful JSON error, and reject ranges whose end would exceed the safe-integer boundary. Preserve successful catalog output and category filtering.

Add node:test cases for defaults, valid offsets, the maximum-limit clamp, zero/negative limits, negative offsets, decimals, junk, empty values, and unsafe integers. Assert invalid requests never access the database. Load the route through in-memory TypeScript transpilation and VM dependency stubs using the existing TypeScript installation; no live services or new dependencies. Run node --test tests/catalog-pagination.test.mjs. No credentials, auth, payments, sends, deploys, migrations, workflows, or package.json changes. Do not commit or push; work on the assigned branch you are on.
